equations.description: Parameterization of the reverse diffusion Markov chain and its Gaussian transition kernel.
equations.context: The joint distribution \(p_\theta(x_{0:T})\) is called the reverse process, and it is defined as a Markov chain with learned Gaussian transitions starting at \(p(x_T)=\mathcal{N}(x_T;0,I)\).
equations.core_reason: This defines the learned generative reverse process that is the backbone of the diffusion model.

Uses the Gaussian transition kernel to sample x_{t-1} = mean + std * noise, with no noise at t=0, directly corresponding to the reverse chain transition.
Initializes x_T from standard normal noise and iteratively applies p_sample to realize the full reverse Markov chain p_\u03b8(x_{0:T}) = p(x_T)\u220f_t p_\u03b8(x_{t-1}|x_t).

equations.code_mapping_summary: Implements the reverse diffusion generative process as a Markov chain by sampling p(x_{t-1} | x_t) with learned mean and variance, and iterating from Gaussian noise at T down to x_0.

equations.latex: q(x_{1:T}\mid x_0) := \prod_{t=1}^{T} q(x_t\mid x_{t-1}),\qquad q(x_t\mid x_{t-1}) := \mathcal{N}\!\bigl(x_t;\sqrt{1-\beta_t}\,x_{t-1},\beta_t I\bigr)
equations.description: Definition of the fixed forward diffusion process used to corrupt data with Gaussian noise.
equations.context: What distinguishes diffusion models from other types of latent variable models is that the approximate posterior \(q(x_{1:T}\mid x_0)\), called the forward process or diffusion process, is fixed to a Markov chain that gradually adds Gaussian noise to the data according to a variance schedule \(\beta_1,\ldots,\beta_T\).
equations.core_reason: This specifies the noising process needed to train and sample from the diffusion model.

code_locations.rationale: Defines the beta_t variance schedule that parameterizes the forward diffusion process.
Stores betas and validates they are in (0,1], setting up the fixed forward chain parameters.

q_sample is the closed-form forward diffusion marginal q(x_t|x_0)=sqrt(alpha_cumprod)*x_0 + sqrt(1-alpha_cumprod)*noise, which directly realizes the Gaussian corruption process implied by the equation.

equations.code_mapping_summary: Implementation of the fixed forward diffusion process q(x_{1:T}\mid x_0) as a Markov noising chain with Gaussian transitions parameterized by a beta schedule, plus the closed-form sampling function q(x_t\mid x_0) used to realize that process in code.

equations.latex: \mathbb{E}\bigl[-\log p_\theta(x_0)\bigr] \le \mathbb{E}_q\!\left[-\log \frac{p_\theta(x_{0:T})}{q(x_{1:T}\mid x_0)}\right] = \mathbb{E}_q\!\left[-\log p(x_T) - \sum_{t\ge 1} \log \frac{p_\theta(x_{t-1}\mid x_t)}{q(x_t\mid x_{t-1})}\right] = L
equations.description: Variational lower bound objective used for training diffusion models.
equations.context: Training is performed by optimizing the usual variational bound on negative log likelihood: \(\mathbb{E}[-\log p_\theta(x_0)] \le \mathbb{E}_q[-\log \frac{p_\theta(x_{0:T})}{q(x_{1:T}\mid x_0)}] = \mathbb{E}_q[-\log p(x_T) - \sum_{t\ge 1} \log \frac{p_\theta(x_{t-1}\mid x_t)}{q(x_t\mid x_{t-1})}] = L\).
equations.core_reason: This is the main training objective from which the method is optimized.

figures.code_mapping_summary: Implementation of the figure’s directed graphical model is reflected in the diffusion process utilities that define the forward noising chain q(x_t|x_0), the reverse/posterior distributions q(x_{t-1}|x_t,x_0) and p(x_{t-1}|x_t), and the sampling loop that traverses timesteps from noisy x_T to clean x_0.
